chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed us of it from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad ibn Qūlawayh, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyād, all together, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī al-Hamadhānī, from ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Khayyāṭ, from Samāʿah ibn Mihrān, from al-Kalbī al-Nassābah, that he asked Abā ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام about nabīdh, and he said:
It is halal. He said: We prepare nabīdh and put into it the dregs and other than that. He said: Fie, fie! That is the foul-smelling khamr.

He said: I said, may I be your ransom, then which nabīdh do you mean? He said: The people of al-Madīnah complained to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم about the change in the water and the corruption of their constitutions, so he ordered them to prepare nabīdh. A man would instruct his servant to prepare it for him, so he would take a handful of dates and cast it into the waterskin; from it was his drink, and from it was his means of purification.
So I said: How many dates were there in the handful? He said: Whatever the hand could carry. I said: One or two? He said: At times it was one, and at times it was two.
I said: And how much did the waterskin hold? He said: Between forty and eighty, and more than that. I said: By which ratls? He said: The ratls of the measure of Iraq.

key_terms.أَرْطَالُ: ratls, units of weight or measure
key_terms.النَّبِيذِ: a date-infused drink prepared by casting dates into water
key_terms.طَهُورُهُ: that by which ritual purification is performed

ai.seo_question: What kind of nabīdh was considered halal and usable for purification in the hadith of al-Istibṣār?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the ruling of nabīdh made from a very small amount of dates placed in water, distinguishing it from foul intoxicating khamr. It also reports that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم permitted such preparation for the people of al-Madīnah due to the condition of their water, and that it was used both for drinking and ritual purification.
